title: github-sts trust policy v1
description:
Trust policy for github-sts. Authored at .github/sts/{app}/{identity}.sts.yaml in a consuming repo (or in the org policy repo for centralised resolution). Controls which OIDC identity may exchange a token for which GitHub App installation token, with which permissions, scoped to which repositories.

Schema source of truth: github.com/Depthmark/github-sts at internal/policy/yaml/schema_v1.json, published to this URL by the documentation site build. Customise by forking that repo, not this URL.

Stability: from first publication the v1 path accepts additive changes only. New optional properties and new permission names may appear; no property is removed, no entry is added to required, and no pattern is tightened. The single exception is a correction that tracks GitHub's own contract, such as a permission level GitHub stops accepting: that is published under v1 because a policy relying on the looser rule was already failing at the mint call. Any other breaking change publishes a v2 path and leaves v1 serving.

not.description: subject and subject_pattern are mutually exclusive. The broker rejects policies that set both.

issuer.description: OIDC issuer URL. Must exactly match the iss claim of the presented token. Examples: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com (GitHub Actions), https://accounts.google.com (Google Workload Identity), https://sts.windows.net/<tenant>/ (Azure AD), https://oidc.eks.<region>.amazonaws.com/id/<id> (AWS EKS).

subject.description: Exact-match subject (sub claim). Mutually exclusive with subject_pattern. Use for tightly scoped identities (e.g., a single workflow on a single ref).

subject_pattern.description: Regex matched against the sub claim. Anchored automatically: the broker compiles ^<pattern>$. Mutually exclusive with subject. Use for ranges (e.g., any branch in a repo) or workflow-level scoping that's not a fixed string.

additionalProperties.description: Regex matched against the claim's value. Anchored automatically: the broker compiles ^<pattern>$. All entries in claim_pattern must match (logical AND).

claim_pattern.description: Per-claim regex constraints applied in addition to subject/subject_pattern. Keys are arbitrary OIDC claim names (e.g., job_workflow_ref, email, oid); values are regex patterns. Useful for narrowing GitHub Actions tokens to a specific reusable workflow or pinning a Google service account email.

github.description: Required for GitHub.com Actions. Binds exact immutable source owner/repository IDs to one exact immutable target repository. IDs are strings and are never interpreted as regular expressions.

audience.description: Required. Exact-match audience (aud claim). Reject tokens minted for other relying parties that share the same issuer. Workflows must request a token with this audience (e.g., core.getIDToken('https://sts.example.com')). A policy without audience would accept tokens minted for any other RP — see security guidance B-2 in the broker's docs.

permissions.description: Required. At least one permission must be granted. Keys are GitHub App installation token permission names and values are the level granted. The accepted levels differ per permission: most take read or write, four also take admin, and a few are read-only or write-only. The broker rejects unknown names and rejects a level GitHub does not accept for that specific permission, so a policy that validates here will not fail the mint call with a 422 over its permission block. GitHub's own OpenAPI description is the source: components.schemas.app-permissions in github/rest-api-description, which is the schema the create-installation-access-token request body declares.

githubID.description: Non-zero decimal GitHub identifier encoded as a quoted string.

sources.description: Exact immutable source repositories authorized by this policy.

target.description: Exact immutable repository for which the broker may mint a token.

readWrite.description: GitHub accepts read or write for this permission.

readWriteAdmin.description: GitHub accepts read, write, or admin for this permission.

readOnly.description: GitHub accepts only read for this permission.

writeOnly.description: GitHub accepts only write for this permission. Requesting read is a 422.
